items.prompt: We’ve seen how to rewrite a fraction with ten on the bottom…  7/10  As an equivalent fraction with a hundred on the bottom.  70/100  We can also go the other way, from one hundred on the bottom to ten on the bottom. My turn first: here is a fraction with a hundred on the bottom. Its equivalent fraction over ten, is this.
items.demo: Its equivalent fraction over ten, is *7/10*.

items.prompt: Watch what I change. Over ten, the equivalent fraction is this.
items.demo: Over ten, the equivalent fraction is *3/10*.

items.prompt: Watch what I change. Again, over ten, the equivalent fraction is this.
items.demo: Again, over ten, the equivalent fraction is *9/10*. Each time, we divide top and bottom by ten.

items.prompt: Your turn. Rewrite forty hundredths as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of ten.
Rewrite sixty hundredths as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of ten.
Rewrite ten hundredths as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of ten.
Rewrite one hundred and twenty hundredths as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of ten.
items.demo: One hundred and twenty hundredths is *12/10*.

items.prompt: Rewrite one hundred hundredths as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of ten.
Rewrite seven hundred thousandths as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of ten.
Can 52/100 be rewritten with ten on the bottom and a whole number on top? How do you know?
items.expected: No. We would need to divide both top and bottom by ten. Fifty-two divided by ten is 5.2, which is not a whole number.
